input.question: Does putting two engines on the same aircraft give it double the thrust?
input.ground_truth: Yes, thrust will double so long as the engines are far enough apart to avoid interacting with each other. Acceleration, top speed and other proformance indicators will not double and may even decreace due to the added weight and drag of a second engine however.

Okay! Imagine you have a toy car, and you put two batteries in it. Does it go twice as fast? Not always! It might go faster, but sometimes the car might get confused or not work right with two batteries.

It’s kind of like that with airplanes and engines. If you put two engines on a plane, sometimes the plane can go faster or carry more stuff, because both engines help push it. But it doesn’t always mean the plane gets *double* the push (that’s called thrust).

Think of it like this: If one engine gives the plane a big push, two engines might give a bigger push, but not always exactly two times bigger. Sometimes the plane can’t use all that extra push because of how it’s built, or the air around it gets crowded. So, two engines don’t always mean double the push!
